title: Pricing stress grid + headcount triage (working notes)
body:
Objective:
Provide an operational, quick-reference stress grid that ties short-term pricing moves to headcount triage options and runway impact. This is a working doc — not final. Focus is on 0–6 month actions that preserve SLA while buying runway if revenue softens.

Quick summary / recommended guardrails (TL;DR):
- If net ARR shock < 5%: tactical pricing promos, hire freeze on non-customer-facing reqs, no involuntary actions.
- If net ARR shock 5–18%: implement targeted price floor increases for low-value routes, accelerate Dedicated upsell offers, pause open non-critical IC hiring, convert 8–12% of contractor hours into short-term redistribution.
- If net ARR shock > 18%: prepare HC reduction scenarios with prioritized role lists + 60/90 day notice templates; enable rapid slab-to-spot pricing toggle and emergency burst-capacity sales push.

Assumptions used for the grid (rough, revise with supply-side team):
- Baseline token mix: 70% generation, 20% embeddings, 10% fine-rerank/other.
- Average token cost to Redwood (after reserved capacity) = $0.0009 / token-equivalent.
- Baseline blended take-rate = 28% (hosted + dedicated margin blended).
- Headcount cost (fully loaded avg) = $210k/year per engineer, $140k/year per non-engine role, contractors averaged $95k equivalent.
- Revenue elasticity per +10% price = -6% demand change (workload-dependent; embeddings more elastic).

Shock scenarios (6-month horizon) — compact grid (scenario / price delta / demand delta / token demand / near-term HC action / approximate monthly cash delta):

Scenario A — Soft wobble (mild)
- Price action: +5% on low-incidence routes (experimental)
- Demand response: -3% overall (embeddings -5%, gen -2%)
- Token demand change: baseline 1.0 -> 0.97
- HC action: hiring freeze on non-customer teams; defer 1 upcoming senior hire (savings ~ $17k/mo)
- Monthly cash pivot: ~-2.5% revenue; net cash loss mitigated by $17k hiring hold

Scenario B — Mid pain (moderate)
- Price action: +10% across starter slabs; targeted discounts removed on legacy customers
- Demand response: -8% overall (embeddings -12%, gen -6%)
- Token demand change: baseline 1.0 -> 0.92
- HC action: pause all non-critical hiring; shift 10% of contractor budget to customer success for upsell motion; freeze bonus pools for Q next quarter (estimated savings $360k/quarter)
- Monthly cash pivot: ~-6% revenue; savings from hiring/contractors offset ~40% of gap.

Scenario C — Severe shock (stress)
- Price action: emergency price floors +15% and temporary surcharge on burst capacity
- Demand response: -20% overall (embeddings -28%, gen -16%)
- Token demand change: baseline 1.0 -> 0.80
- HC action: prioritized triage list (see below) -> implement hiring pause + 15% FTE reduction if runway < 9 months; reassign infra SREs to ops-critical windows; contract pool cut by 40%
- Monthly cash pivot: ~-18% revenue; with headcount reduction(s) runway extends by ~3–4 months depending on severity

Prioritized headcount triage (for scenario planning) — rules and ranking:
1) Protect frontline SRE / infra (inc. dedicated capacity ops) and sales-engineering that enable committed revenue.
2) Defer product incubations and non-revenue feature squads first.
3) Prefer contractor reductions before full-time layoffs when functionally possible.
4) Preserve core model onboarding and quantization infra (long-term cost savings) but slow long-tail R&D ramp.
5) Use voluntary separation + partial severance + redeployment windows to reduce involuntary layoffs.

Sample triage matrix (flattened, used as quick lookup):
- Role bucket: Sales/CS (protect up to 95%), SRE/Infra (protect 90%), Serving runtime eng (protect 80%), Product growth/incubation (cut first up to 60%), Research/applied-ml (protect core 60%, cut long-tail), Contractors (cut up to 40% early)

Short checklist for Finance + People Ops to operationalize a mid-severity move (B->C trigger):
- [ ] Recompute token burn vs existing committed revenue (run daily for 14 days)
- [ ] Activate price floor toggle in billing (engineer: billing-toggle-flag PR reference)
- [ ] Notify Sales and CS with planned customer messaging draft (owner: Jasmine P)
- [ ] Launch targeted upsell bundle for Dedicated seats (owner: Marco R)
- [ ] Cascade hiring freeze memos + create exceptions process (owner: People Ops)
- [ ] Prepare contractor re-engagement plan for critical path work (owner: Eng leads)
- [ ] Legal review for layoff notice templates (owner: Legal)
- [ ] Draft investor note for >12% shock scenario (owner: Priya)

Customer messaging notes (draft bullets):
- We are streamlining slab pricing and introducing a short-term burst surcharge to ensure service reliability for committed customers.
- Offer transitional credits for multi-month committed purchases and straightforward upgrade paths to Dedicated pools.
- Keep message channelized: customers on Enterprise get 2-week prior notice + bespoke mitigation offers; self-serve get banner/console notice.

Open questions / data pulls needed (priority order):
1) Token-level elasticity by enterprise cohort (ask analytics: two-week slice of route-level take, per-customer price responsiveness).
2) Marginal GPU hourly cost across regions and instance types (ops to provide 7-day moving average).
3) Current contractor schedules and scopings to identify reducible workstreams.
4) Legal constraints per region for 60/90-day notice rules.

Decision thresholds (examples):
- If trailing 30d net revenue decline > 12% AND projected runway < 10 months -> trigger mid-severity playbook and notify execs.
- If trailing 30d revenue decline > 20% -> trigger emergency playbook (Scenario C) and immediate board briefing.

Appendix: quick math examples (simplified)
- Baseline monthly revenue (example): $25M ARR -> ~$2.083M/mo. A -6% demand shift (Scenario B) reduces monthly revenue by ~125k.
- Monthly staff savings from pausing 8 open roles (average fully loaded $18k/month per role) -> ~$144k/mo. Combine with contractor reallocation (~$50k/mo) -> covers ~155k of gap in example.

Notes and breadcrumbs:
- Jira ticket FIN-3421 contains the live simulation workbook and the latest elasticity parameters.
- Confluence page FIN-ops/pricing-guardrails has historic experiments (June–Oct 2026) and prior customer communications.
- Quick demo stripe toggle flag: billing-toggle-flag-2026 (engineering PR link in linked_artifacts).

Next steps (immediate 7d):
- Priya: coordinate daily revenue slice + run 7-day elasticity split by cohort (owner)
- Jasmine: draft customer comm for enterprise tier and prepare CS playbook (owner)
- Marco: prepare Dedicated upsell pack + price/bundle options (owner)
- Liam: implement a read-only snapshot of contractor spend per squad (owner)

Scratch / working thoughts (brain dump):
- Consider a blended microdiscount for high-volume embeddings customers with SLA tie-in (gives us ability to push price floors elsewhere).
- A short-term surcharge tied to peak token windows (time-of-day) could be rolled out to reduce peak capacity costs without global price increases — ops complexity tradeoff.
- Test a 30-day limited price increase on a random 5% customer sample and measure churn over 30/60/90.

End of notes.

(Version history: draft v0.2 — added triage matrix and checklist 2027-01-28)
